cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1:1-2). Some people there are troubling the believers, trying to compel them to be circumcised and keep the law (Galatians 1:7; 6:12-13). Now Paul says it plain: "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free."

cards.question: Christ has set them free. So what does Paul tell the Galatians to do now?

answers.text: Work hard to earn their freedom

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that now they're free, the Galatians could never be weighed down by a yoke of slavery again.

cards.text: Then Paul puts his own NAME on the next line about circumcision: "Take notice: I, Paul, tell you..." Friend, when somebody signs their name in the middle of a letter, you set the cookie dough down and LISTEN.

cards.question: If the Galatians let themselves be circumcised, what does Paul say Christ will be worth to them?
True or false: Paul says a man who gets himself circumcised is obligated to obey just that one command and nothing more.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to anyone trying to be justified by the law. Oh, he's talking to them DIRECTLY now, friend, no hiding behind the oven.

cards.question: What does Paul say about people who are trying to be justified by the law?

answers.text: They have been severed from Christ
They have drawn closer to Christ

cards.text: Paul tells them, "you have fallen away from grace." But he and the believers wait for the hope of righteousness, and they wait eagerly, through the Spirit.

cards.question: Paul says that by ___ they eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.
In Christ Jesus, Paul says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. So what does matter?

answers.text: Coming from the right family line

cards.text: Paul writes, "You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?" That's me sliding a full tray toward the oven, smooth, SMOOTH, and then a baker parks a mixing bowl right in my path.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the persuasion that's slowing the Galatians down comes from the One who calls them.

cards.text: Then Paul pulls a picture straight out of MY kitchen: leaven in the dough! I have waited this ENTIRE letter for somebody to talk dough, friend.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through how much of the dough?
Paul is confident in the Lord that the Galatians will take no other view. What does he say about the one troubling them, whoever he may be?

answers.text: He will be let off free
He will be put in charge

cards.text: Then Paul asks the brothers something. If he's still preaching circumcision, why is he still being persecuted?

cards.question: Paul asks why he's still being persecuted if he's still preaching circumcision. True or false: Paul is admitting he still preaches circumcision.

cards.text: And if he were, Paul says, "In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished."
Then Paul gets blunt about the people agitating the Galatians. He says he wishes they would go ahead and emasculate themselves.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers they were called to freedom. True or false: he says they should use that freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, "serve one another in love." Free to SERVE, friend, and nobody serves faster than a stamper with a mustache full of cookie boxes.

cards.question: Paul says the entire law is fulfilled in a single decree. Which one?
Paul warns that if the Galatians keep on biting and devouring one another, they will be ___ by one another.

findings.problem: The card says the troublers are 'trying to compel them to be circumcised and keep the law (Galatians 1:7; 6:12-13).' Galatians 6:12 says they are trying to compel the Galatians to be circumcised, but neither cited verse says they compel them to keep the law. Galatians 6:13 says the troublers don't keep the law themselves. 'And keep the law' stretches the cited texts.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: 'No hiding behind the oven' puts Paul into Papa Dorin's bakery. That blends the kitchen comparison with the Bible setting. The image also doesn't land, because nothing in the passage suggests Paul was hiding or holding back.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: the two quoted sentences from 5:7 plus the tray joke. The quote or the joke needs trimming, or the beat needs splitting.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card is a flat restatement with no Papa Dorin voice ('Then Paul asks the brothers something.'). The very next choice card repeats its content word for word, so the card adds nothing. Cards 8 and 9 that follow are also plain retelling, which leaves a dry run of cards through 5:11-12.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The joke 'nobody serves faster than a stamper with a mustache full of cookie boxes' puns on serving food and is about speed. Paul's action is serving one another in love, so the comparison doesn't share the core action. It also reads as a boast instead of Papa Dorin being the joke.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card uses facts from Galatians 1:1-2, 1:7 and 6:12-13 and cites them inline in the card text. The card's 'verses' field lists only Galatians 5:1, and bakers would see raw references in the story text.
findings.question: When a story card uses facts from outside the passage, should their references go inline in the card text, in the 'verses' field, or somewhere else?
